# AI ROI Calculator by OptimNow

> Free web application to calculate return on investment for AI and LLM implementations,
> using a 3-layer cost framework that separates model inference, orchestration harness,
> and business value. Built and maintained by OptimNow, a cloud and AI FinOps advisory.

The calculator itself is a client-side React application, so its interface is rendered in
the browser. The complete mathematical specification behind it is published as a static
page and is the best source for how any of these figures are derived.

## Documentation

- [Methodology](https://airoicalculator.optimnow.io/methodology.html): the complete
  specification — 3-layer cost model, all four value methods, break-even and payback
  derivations, sensitivity analysis, and a worked end-to-end example with real numbers.
- [Calculator](https://airoicalculator.optimnow.io/): the interactive tool, with 11 preset
  use cases and live model prices.
- [Source](https://github.com/OptimNow/ai-roi-calculator): TypeScript implementation of the
  engine described above.

## Related

- [OptimToken](https://optimtoken.optimnow.io): the model price catalog this calculator
  consumes — per-million-token input, output, cache-read and batch rates across providers,
  refreshed daily.
- [OptimNow](https://www.optimnow.io): cloud and AI financial management advisory.

## What it computes

- Layer 1, infrastructure: token-priced or per-call model inference, blended across two
  routing slots, with prompt-cache and batch-API rates and a retry multiplier.
- Layer 2, harness: orchestration, retrieval, tool APIs, logging, guardrails, egress and
  storage, plus an operational overhead multiplier. Layer 2 is cumulative — it contains
  Layer 1.
- Layer 3, business value, by one of four methods: Cost Displacement, Revenue Uplift,
  Retention Uplift, Premium Monetization.
- Derived metrics: ROI percentage, monthly net benefit, payback period, break-even volume,
  and a four-variable sensitivity analysis.

## Notes

- Free, no account, no data collection. Scenarios are stored in the browser only.
- Self-hosted GPU amortization is not modeled; token-based and flat per-request billing are.
